raw: {"analysis":"Response SZR correctly identifies that the dual approval requirement maps to the Backend Lead and Head of Trust & Safety, and properly escalates the 'allow on outage' fallback as a security risk requiring Trust & Safety sign-off before implementation. Response CBV incorrectly repurposes the Head of Trust & Safety as a code reviewer rather than a deployment approver, and its rollback plan is dangerously flawed—reverting to disable the fraud check returns the system to pure fail-open behavior, which is the exact opposite of safe rollback given the irreversibility constraint. SZR also better addresses the rate limit risk by flagging it as a critical constraint requiring staged testing, while CBV's token bucket approach is reasonable but its load test plan of spiking to 550 RPS risks triggering the IP ban it's supposed to prevent.","verdict":"SZR"}
